newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB - Russia may boost non-CIS wheat imports.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Russia may boost non-CIS wheat imports.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIA LIKELY TO INCREASE NON-CIS WHEAT IMPORTS DUE TO CIS HIGH PRICES
MOSCOW, Nov 20 - Normally, with the beginning of a new crop year, Russia's grain imports decline to their lowest level of the year.
However, Russia's wheat imports in July-September remained close to levels seen in the last three months of 1995/96 (April-June).
At the same time, some new trends in Russia's wheat imports in 1996/97 can be discerned:
- Wheat and flour deliveries from the countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), particularly flour from Ukraine, have declined on the previous quarter (April-June);

- Despite low export stocks in last year's major suppliers (East European states), Russia has increased its wheat and flour imports from third countries. Increased deliveries from India, Finland and Sweden have diversified the wheat import pattern.
On the one hand, these trends reflect a tight grain supply in Russia coupled with high domestic prices for milling wheat.
Despite the completion of the harvest, milling wheat prices remain between $190-200 per tonne at Russian silos.
On the other hand, the above trends indicate low export stocks in Russia's major suppliers - Ukraine and Kazakhstan.
Kazakh milling wheat now costs $160-175 at silos.
Given that, Russian buyers are likely to start seeking Western wheat, particularly thanks to a further decline in wheat prices on Western markets.
